claim: Statement. With k10 = 0, under the threshold law (kr ≥ 1) or mass action, the open level has unbounded solutions. Proof. section: The saturation mechanism in the working turnover grammar / S5. Cycling needs a lag (class A, with an exploratory check)
claim: Statement. On a closed level with k1 = k7 = 0 and L(0) = P(0) = 0, C(t) is monotone and converges to a balance: no overshoot and no cycle. Proof. L and P stay 0, and V = T − C, so dC/dt = −k2·C + (k10 + k3·F(C/T))·(T − C) is a scalar autonomous equation, whose solutions are monotone. ∎ If L(0) or P(0) is positive, both decay exponentially and the limit set lies in the same scalar system. So on a closed level, cycling needs a delayed route back through L or P. This proves [theorem, model] the line 'Cycling around balance requires a lagged counter-process' on 'Self-limiting growth', for this grammar.
